      "environment.py": "\"\"\"Implements the Tic-Tac-Toe game logic and a Gymnasium-compatible wrapper.\"\"\"\n\nimport gymnasium as gym\nfrom typing import Tuple, Optional\nimport numpy as np\n\n\nclass TicTacToeEnv(gym.Env):\n    \"\"\"A Gymnasium environment for the Game of Tic-Tac-Toe.\n    \n    The board is represented as a 1D array of size 9 (3x3 flattened), \n    where cells contain 0 (empty), 1 (player X), or -1 (player O).\n    Player X always moves first.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    metadata = {\"render_modes\": [\"human\", \"ansi\"]}\n\n    def __init__(self, render_mode: Optional[str] = None):\n        \"\"\"Initialize the environment.\n        \n        Args:\n            render_mode: Rendering mode string. Defaults to None (no rendering).\n        \"\"\"\n        super().__init__()\n        self.render_mode = render_mode\n        self.board_size = 9\n        self.observation_space = gym.spaces.Box(\n            low=-1, high=1, shape=(self.board_size,), dtype=np.int8\n        )\n        self.action_space = gym.spaces.Discrete(self.board_size)\n        self._state: np.ndarray = None\n        self._done: bool = False\n        self._current_player: int = 1  # 1 for X, -1 for O\n        self._seed_rng = np.random.default_rng()\n\n    def reset(\n        self, \n        seed: Optional[int] = None \n    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, dict]:\n        \"\"\"Resets the environment to the initial state.\n        \n        Args:\n            seed: Optional random seed for reproducibility. Defaults to None.\n            \n        Returns:\n            observation: The initial board state (np.ndarray of shape (9,) with dtype int8).\n            info: Auxiliary diagnostic information (empty dict).\n        \"\"\"\n        super().reset(seed=seed)\n        self._state = np.zeros(self.board_size, dtype=np.int8)\n        self._done = False\n        self._current_player = 1\n        return self._state.copy(), {}\n\n    def step(\n        self, \n        action: int \n    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, float, bool, bool, dict]:\n        \"\"\"Performs a single environment step.\n        \n        Args:\n            action: An integer in [0, 8] representing the cell index to place a mark.\n            \n        Returns:\n            observation: The new board state (np.ndarray).\n            reward: Reward for the current player (+1 for win, 0 for draw, -1 for loss).\n            terminated: Boolean indicating if the game has ended due to win or loss.\n            truncated: Boolean indicating if the episode was truncated (e.g., max steps). Always False here.\n            info: Auxiliary diagnostic information including if the action was legal and whose turn it is.\n            \n        Raises:\n            ValueError: If the action is invalid (cell already occupied).\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._done:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"Episode must be reset before stepping again.\")\n\n        if not self.action_space.contains(action):\n            raise ValueError(f\"Invalid action {action}. Must be in [0, 8].\")\n\n        if self._state[action] != 0:\n            # Penalty for invalid move: immediate loss\n            reward = -1.0\n            terminated = True\n            info = {\n                \"valid_action\": False,\n                \"player_turn\": self._current_player,\n                \"board_copy\": self._state.copy()\n            }\n            return self._state, reward, terminated, False, info\n\n        # Apply move\n        self._state[action] = self._current_player\n        \n        # Check for termination\n        win = self._check_win(self._current_player)\n        if win:\n            reward = 1.0\n            terminated = True\n        elif np.all(self._state != 0):\n            # Draw\n            reward = 0.5  # Standard convention: half point for draw, or 0. Let's use 0.5 to distinguish from loss (-1) visually if needed, but typically 0 for draw in zero-sum games is better. \n                           # However, to make it clear it's not a win for either:\n            reward = 0.0\n            terminated = True\n        else:\n            reward = 0.0\n            terminated = False\n            self._current_player *= -1\n\n        info = {\n            \"valid_action\": True,\n            \"player_turn\": self._current_player if not terminated else 0,\n            \"board_copy\": self._state.copy()\n        }\n\n        return self._state, reward, terminated, False, info\n\n    def _check_win(self, player: int) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Check if the specified player has won.\n        \n        Args:\n            player: The player identifier (1 or -1).\n            \n        Returns:\n            True if the player has three in a row, False otherwise.\n        \"\"\"\n        b = self._state.reshape(3, 3)\n        # Rows\n        if np.any(b.sum(axis=1) == player * 3):\n            return True\n        # Cols\n        if np.any(b.sum(axis=0) == player * 3):\n            return True\n        # Diagonals\n        if b[0, 0] == player and b[1, 1] == player and b[2, 2] == player:\n            return True\n        if b[0, 2] == player and b[1, 1] == player and b[2, 0] == player:\n            return True\n        return False\n",
      "agent.py": "\"\"\"Implements the Q-Learning agent class with standard exploration-exploitation logic (epsilon-greedy).\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom typing import Optional, Tuple\n\n# Avoid circular import issues by using string annotation or lazy import if necessary,\n# but here we assume environment is available in the namespace when this file is imported.\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv\n\n# --- Constants ---\nDEFAULT_ALPHA: float = 0.1\nDEFAULT_GAMMA: float = 0.9\nDEFAULT_EPSILON_START: float = 1.0\nDEFAULT_EPSILON_END: float = 0.05\n\n\nclass QLearningAgent:\n    \"\"\"A tabular Q-Learning agent for Tic-Tac-Toe.\n    \n    The agent maintains a Q-table mapping states (board configurations) to action values.\n    It uses an epsilon-greedy policy for exploration.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        env: TicTacToeEnv,\n        alpha: float = DEFAULT_ALPHA,\n        gamma: float = DEFAULT_GAMMA,\n        epsilon: float = DEFAULT_EPSILON_START,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the Q-Learning agent.\n        \n        Args:\n            env: The TicTacToe environment instance. Used to determine action space size.\n            alpha: The learning rate for Q-value updates. Defaults to 0.1.\n            gamma: The discount factor for future rewards. Defaults to 0.9.\n            epsilon: The initial exploration rate (probability of choosing a random action).\n                     Defaults to 1.0 (pure exploration initially).\n        \"\"\"\n        self.env = env\n        self.alpha = alpha\n        self.gamma = gamma\n        self.epsilon = epsilon\n        \n        # Action space size is determined by the environment (9 cells)\n        num_actions = env.action_space.n\n        # Initialize Q-table with zeros. Key: state tuple, Value: array of Q-values.\n        self.q_table: dict[Tuple[int, ...], np.ndarray] = {}\n        \n        # Use modern numpy random generator to avoid AttributeError on .integers()\n        self.rng = np.random.default_rng()\n\n    def act(self, state: np.ndarray) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select an action for the given state using the epsilon-greedy policy.\n        \n        If a random number is less than epsilon, a random valid action is selected.\n        Otherwise, the action with the highest Q-value is selected. Ties are broken randomly.\n        \n        Args:\n            state: The current environment observation (np.ndarray of shape (9,) with dtype int8).\n                   Must contain only values from {-1, 0, 1}.\n                   \n        Returns:\n            action: An integer in [0, 8] representing the chosen cell index.\n        \"\"\"\n        state_key = tuple(state)\n        \n        # Initialize Q-values for new states\n        if state_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[state_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        \n        # Epsilon-greedy action selection\n        if self.rng.random() < self.epsilon:\n            return int(self.rng.integers(0, self.env.action_space.n))\n        else:\n            q_values = self.q_table[state_key]\n            # Find all actions with the maximum Q-value\n            max_q = np.max(q_values)\n            max_actions = np.where(q_values == max_q)[0]\n            # Randomly choose one of the best actions\n            return int(max_actions[self.rng.integers(0, len(max_actions))])\n\n    def update(\n        self,\n        state: np.ndarray,\n        action: int,\n        reward: float,\n        next_state: np.ndarray,\n        done: bool,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Update the Q-value for the given state-action pair.\n        \n        Uses the standard Q-Learning update rule:\n        Q(s, a) <- Q(s, a) + alpha * (reward + gamma * max_a' Q(s', a') - Q(s, a))\n        \n        Args:\n            state: The previous environment observation.\n            action: The action taken by the agent.\n            reward: The reward received from the environment.\n            next_state: The new environment observation after taking the action.\n            done: Boolean indicating if the episode has terminated.\n        \"\"\"\n        s_key = tuple(state)\n        a_next_key = tuple(next_state)\n        \n        # Initialize Q-values for the next state if it hasn't been visited\n        if a_next_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[a_next_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        # Ensure s_key is also initialized to be safe (though act usually does this)\n        if s_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[s_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        \n        current_q = self.q_table[s_key][action]\n        \n        if done:\n            target = reward\n        else:\n            max_next_q = np.max(self.q_table[a_next_key])\n            target = reward + self.gamma * max_next_q\n            \n        self.q_table[s_key][action] += self.alpha * (target - current_q)\n",
      "baseline_agent.py": "\"\"\"Implements the random baseline agent that selects uniformly from valid moves.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom typing import Optional, TYPE_CHECKING\n\nif TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from environment import TicTacToeEnv\n\n\nclass RandomAgent:\n    \"\"\"A dummy agent that chooses a legal move at random for baseline comparison.\n\n    Attributes:\n        env: The Tic-Tac-Toe environment instance used to determine board size and rules.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, env: \"TicTacToeEnv\") -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the random agent.\n\n        Args:\n            env: The Tic-TacToe environment instance. Stored to query valid actions.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.env = env\n\n    def act(self, state: np.ndarray) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select a valid action uniformly at random from the legal moves in ``state``.\n\n        Args:\n            state: Current board observation (numpy array of shape (9,)).\n                   Must contain values 0 (empty), 1 (X), -1 (O).\n\n        Returns:\n            action: Integer index in [0, 8] corresponding to an empty cell on the board.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Identify empty cells (value == 0)\n        empty_indices = np.where(state == 0)[0]\n        if len(empty_indices) == 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"No empty cells available for action.\")\n        return int(np.random.choice(empty_indices))\n",
      "experiment.py": "\"\"\"Orchestrates the training of the Q-Learning agent and its evaluation against both itself (during play) and the random baseline, aggregating results into a CSV file.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import List, Tuple, Dict\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv\nfrom agent import QLearningAgent\nfrom baseline_agent import RandomAgent\n\n# --- Constants ---\nN_EPISODES: int = 1000\nRANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES: int = 1000\nSEED: int = 42\nEpsilonDecayRate: float = 0.995\nMinEpsilon: float = 0.01\nOUTPUT_CSV: str = \"results.csv\"\nWORKSPACE_ROOT: Path = Path(\".\")\n\n\ndef run_experiment() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run the full reinforcement learning experiment and save results to CSV.\n\n    This function performs three main phases:\n    1. Training: The Q-Learning agent plays against a random opponent for \n       ``N_EPISODES`` episodes, updating its Q-table after each move.\n    2. Baseline Evaluation: A game played between two RandomAgents is simulated \n       for ``RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES`` games to establish a win/draw/loss distribution \n       for purely random play.\n    3. Final Evaluation: The trained Q-Learning agent plays against the same \n       RandomAgent for ``RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES`` games to measure its performance.\n\n    Results are aggregated into rows with columns: \n    ``method, metric, value, std_dev, n_runs``.\n    Methods are \"Q-Learning_vs_Random\" and \"Random_vs_Random\". Metrics are \n    \"win_rate\", \"draw_rate\", \"loss_rate\" (relative to the agent named first). \n\n    The output CSV is written to the workspace root at ``results.csv``.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = TicTacToeEnv()\n    \n    # Initialize Q-Learning Agent\n    agent = QLearningAgent(\n        env=env,\n        epsilon=1.0\n    )\n    \n    # Initialize Random Agents for baseline and evaluation\n    random_agent_eval = RandomAgent(env)\n    random_agent_baseline_1 = RandomAgent(env)\n    random_agent_baseline_2 = RandomAgent(env)\n    \n    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)\n\n    # --- Phase 1: Training ---\n    for episode in range(N_EPISODES):\n        state, _ = env.reset(seed=SEED + episode)\n        done = False\n        \n        while not done:\n            action = agent.act(state)\n            next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            agent.update(state, action, reward, next_state, done)\n            state = next_state\n            \n            # Decay epsilon\n            if agent.epsilon > MinEpsilon:\n                agent.epsilon *= EpsilonDecayRate\n\n    # --- Phase 2: Baseline Evaluation (Random vs Random) ---\n    baseline_results = _evaluate_agent(\n        env=env,\n        p1_agent=random_agent_baseline_1,\n        p2_agent=random_agent_baseline_2,\n        n_games=RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES,\n        rng=rng\n    )\n    \n    # --- Phase 3: Trained Agent Evaluation (Q-Learning vs Random) ---\n    trained_results = _evaluate_agent(\n        env=env,\n        p1_agent=agent,\n        p2_agent=random_agent_eval,\n        n_games=RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES,\n        rng=rng\n    )\n\n    # --- Aggregation and CSV Writing ---\n    rows: List[List[str]] = []\n\n    # Baseline Rows (Random vs Random)\n    rows.append([\"Random_vs_Random\", \"win_rate\", f\"{baseline_results['p1_wins'] / RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES:.4f}\", \"0\", str(RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES)])\n    rows.append([\"Random_vs_Random\", \"draw_rate\", f\"{baseline_results['draws'] / RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES:.4f}\", \"0\", str(RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES)])\n    rows.append([\"Random_vs_Random\", \"loss_rate\", f\"{baseline_results['p1_losses'] / RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES:.4f}\", \"0\", str(RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES)])\n\n    # Q-Learning Rows (Trained vs Random)\n    rows.append([\"Q-Learning_vs_Random\", \"win_rate\", f\"{trained_results['p1_wins'] / RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES:.4f}\", \"0\", str(RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES)])\n    rows.append([\"Q-Learning_vs_Random\", \"draw_rate\", f\"{trained_results['draws'] / RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES:.4f}\", \"0\", str(RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES)])\n    rows.append([\"Q-Learning_vs_Random\", \"loss_rate\", f\"{trained_results['p1_losses'] / RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES:.4f}\", \"0\", str(RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES)])\n\n    output_path = WORKSPACE_ROOT / OUTPUT_CSV\n    with open(output_path, mode='w', newline='') as csvfile:\n        writer = csv.writer(csvfile)\n        writer.writerow([\"method\", \"metric\", \"value\", \"std_dev\", \"n_runs\"])\n        writer.writerows(rows)\n\n\ndef _evaluate_agent(\n    env: TicTacToeEnv,\n    p1_agent, \n    p2_agent,\n    n_games: int,\n    rng: np.random.Generator\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Evaluate an agent playing as player 1 against another agent (player 2).\n\n    Args:\n        env: The TicTacToe environment instance.\n        p1_agent: The agent playing as Player X (moves first). Must have ``act(state)``.\n        p2_agent: The agent playing as Player O. Must have ``act(state)``.\n        n_games: Number of games to simulate.\n        rng: Random number generator for reproducibility.\n\n    Returns:\n        A dictionary with keys 'p1_wins', 'p2_wins', 'draws', each mapping to the \n        count of such outcomes observed during the evaluation.\n    \"\"\"\n    p1_wins = 0\n    p2_wins = 0\n    draws = 0\n\n    for i in range(n_games):\n        state, _ = env.reset(seed=rng.integers(0, 10000))\n        done = False\n        last_winner = None \n\n        while not done:\n            if env._current_player == 1:\n                action = p1_agent.act(state)\n            else:\n                action = p2_agent.act(state)\n                \n            next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            \n            # Determine who got what reward. \n            # Reward is from the perspective of the player making the move.\n            if terminated:\n                if reward == 1.0:\n                    # The current mover won\n                    if env._current_player != (-2): # Check logic below carefully based on env step implementation\n                        # In TicTacToeEnv.step, reward is given to self._current_player who just moved.\n                        # But after the move, _current_player switches or stays? \n                        # Env code: self._state[action] = self._current_player. Then checks win. \n                        # If win, reward=1.0 for self._current_player (who just moved).\n                        last_winner = env._current_player if not terminated else None \n                        # Actually, the `info` or return value is key. Let's use simpler logic:\n                        # The player who made the move 'action' receives 'reward'.\n                        # If reward == 1, they won. If reward == -1 (against them? No, env says -1 for loss).\n                        # TicTacToeEnv step: \n                        # win check on `self._current_player` (the mover). If win, reward=1.\n                        # So if reward is 1, the mover won. \n                        if env._current_player == 1: p1_wins += 1\n                        else: p2_wins += 1\n                    else:\n                        # Edge case handling for invalid moves resulting in immediate loss (-1)\n                        # If action was invalid, reward=-1 for mover. So mover lost.\n                        if env._current_player == 1: p1_wins += 1\n                        else: p2_wins += 1\n                elif reward == -1.0:\n                    # The current mover lost (invalid move or opponent won previously? No, immediate loss here)\n                    if env._current_player == 1: p2_wins += 1\n                    else: p1_wins += 1\n                else:\n                    # Draw\n                    draws += 1\n            \n            state = next_state\n\n    return {\n        \"p1_wins\": p1_wins,\n        \"p2_wins\": p2_wins,\n        \"draws\": draws\n    }",
      "plots.py": "\"\"\"Reads experimental results from CSV and generates visualizations of learning curves and win rate comparisons.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nfrom typing import List\n\nimport matplotlib\nmatplotlib.use('Agg')\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nimport seaborn as sns\n\n# Constants for experiment reproducibility and styling\nFIGURE_DIR: str = \"figures\"\nRESULTS_FILE: str = \"results.csv\"\n\n\ndef generate_plots() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Generate plots from experimental results and save them to disk.\n\n    Reads the ``results.csv`` file (written by :func:`experiment.run_experiment`) \n    which must contain columns: 'method', 'metric', 'value'. The CSV is expected to \n    contain rows for win_rate, draw_rate, loss_rate, mean_reward, and std_dev for \n    each method (e.g., 'q_learning', 'random_baseline').\n\n    Creates two figures:\n    1. **Distribution Comparison**: A grouped bar chart comparing the rates of \n       winning, drawing, and losing between the Q-Learning agent and the Baseline.\n    2. **Reward Statistics**: A bar chart comparing the mean reward and standard \n       deviation between the methods.\n\n    Saves figures to ``figures/`` directory (creating it if necessary).\n    \"\"\"\n    # Load data\n    if not os.path.exists(RESULTS_FILE):\n        raise FileNotFoundError(\n            f\"Results file '{RESULTS_FILE}' not found. Run experiment first.\"\n        )\n    \n    df: pd.DataFrame = pd.read_csv(RESULTS_FILE)\n    \n    # Ensure columns exist\n    required_cols: List[str] = ['method', 'metric', 'value']\n    for col in required_cols:\n        if col not in df.columns:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Missing required column '{col}' in {RESULTS_FILE}\")\n\n    # Prepare directories\n    os.makedirs(FIGURE_DIR, exist_ok=True)\n\n    # --- Plot 1: Win/Loss/Draw Distribution Comparison ---\n    _plot_distribution_comparison(df)\n\n    # --- Plot 2: Mean Reward and Std Dev Bar Chart ---\n    _plot_reward_metrics(df)\n\n\ndef _plot_distribution_comparison(df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Visualize win, draw, and loss rates for each method.\n    \n    Args:\n        df: DataFrame containing aggregated results from experiment.csv.\n            Must contain rows for 'win_rate', 'draw_rate', 'loss_rate' per method.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Filter for distribution metrics\n    dist_metrics: List[str] = ['win_rate', 'draw_rate', 'loss_rate']\n    df_dist: pd.DataFrame = df[df['metric'].isin(dist_metrics)].copy()\n    \n    if df_dist.empty:\n        print(\"Warning: No distribution metrics found in results for plotting.\")\n        return\n\n    # Pivot to get rates as columns indexed by method\n    plot_data: pd.DataFrame = df_dist.pivot(index='method', columns='metric', values='value')\n    \n    # Reindex to ensure correct order if some methods miss a metric (unlikely in this harness)\n    for m in dist_metrics:\n        if m not in plot_data.columns:\n            plot_data[m] = 0.0\n    \n    plot_data = plot_data[dist_metrics]\n\n    ax: plt.Axes\n    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n    \n    # Plot grouped bars\n    x_vals: np.ndarray = np.arange(len(plot_data.index))\n    width: float = 0.25\n    methods: List[str] = plot_data.index.tolist()\n    metric_colors = {\n        'win_rate': '#1f77b4',\n        'draw_rate': '#ff7f0e',\n        'loss_rate': '#d62728'\n    }\n\n    for i, metric in enumerate(dist_metrics):\n        if metric in plot_data.columns:\n            ax.bar(\n                x_vals + i * width - width,\n                plot_data[metric],\n                width,\n                label=metric.replace('_', ' ').title(),\n                color=metric_colors[metric],\n                edgecolor='black'\n            )\n    \n    ax.set_xticks(x_vals)\n    ax.set_xticklabels([m.replace('_', '\\n') for m in methods], fontsize=10)\n    ax.set_ylabel('Rate (0-1)')\n    ax.set_title('Win, Draw, and Loss Rates Comparison')\n    ax.legend(loc='lower right')\n    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05)\n    ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n\n    plt.tight_layout()\n    plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURE_DIR, 'distribution_comparison.png'), dpi=150)\n    plt.close(fig)\n\n\ndef _plot_reward_metrics(df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Visualize Mean Reward and Std Dev for each method.\n    \n    Args:\n        df: DataFrame containing aggregated results from experiment.csv.\n            Must contain rows for 'mean_reward' and 'std_dev' per method.\n    \"\"\"\n    reward_metrics: List[str] = ['mean_reward', 'std_dev']\n    df_reward: pd.DataFrame = df[df['metric'].isin(reward_metrics)].copy()\n\n    if df_reward.empty:\n        print(\"Warning: No reward metrics found in results for plotting.\")\n        return\n\n    # Pivot\n    plot_data: pd.DataFrame = df_reward.pivot(index='method', columns='metric', values='value')\n    \n    # Handle missing std_dev (often 0 or not computed if n_runs=1)\n    if 'std_dev' not in plot_data.columns:\n        plot_data['std_dev'] = 0.0\n        print(\"Note: Standard deviation data was missing, defaulted to 0.0.\")\n    \n    plot_data = plot_data[['mean_reward', 'std_dev']]\n\n    ax: plt.Axes\n    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n    \n    x_vals: np.ndarray = np.arange(len(plot_data.index))\n    width: float = 0.35\n\n    bars1 = ax.bar(\n        x_vals - width/2,\n        plot_data['mean_reward'],\n        width,\n        label='Mean Reward',\n        color='#1f77b4',\n        edgecolor='black'\n    )\n    \n    # Plot error bars or a secondary bar for std_dev. A secondary bar is clearer for magnitude.\n    bars2 = ax.bar(\n        x_vals + width/2,\n        plot_data['std_dev'],\n        width,\n        label='Std Dev',\n        color='#ff7f0e',\n        edgecolor='black'\n    )\n\n    ax.set_xticks(x_vals)\n    ax.set_xticklabels([m.replace('_', '\\n') for m in plot_data.index], fontsize=10)\n    ax.set_ylabel('Value')\n    ax.set_title('Mean Reward and Standard Deviation')\n    ax.legend(loc='best')\n    ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n\n    plt.tight_layout()\n    plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURE_DIR, 'reward_metrics.png'), dpi=150)\n    plt.close(fig)"
    },
    "academic_blueprint": {

  "existing_content": "\"\"\"Implements the Q-Learning agent class with standard exploration-exploitation logic (epsilon-greedy).\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\nimport numpy as np\nfrom typing import Optional, Tuple\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv\nDEFAULT_ALPHA: float = 0.1\nDEFAULT_GAMMA: float = 0.9\nDEFAULT_EPSILON_START: float = 1.0\nDEFAULT_EPSILON_END: float = 0.05\n\nclass QLearningAgent:\n    \"\"\"A tabular Q-Learning agent for Tic-Tac-Toe.\n    \n    The agent maintains a Q-table mapping states (board configurations) to action values.\n    It uses an epsilon-greedy policy for exploration.\n    \"\"\"\n    env: 'object'\n    alpha: 'object'\n    gamma: 'object'\n    epsilon: 'object'\n    q_table: 'dict[Tuple[int, ...], np.ndarray]'\n    rng: 'object'\n\n    def __init__(self, env: TicTacToeEnv, alpha: float=DEFAULT_ALPHA, gamma: float=DEFAULT_GAMMA, epsilon: float=DEFAULT_EPSILON_START) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the Q-Learning agent.\n\nArgs:\n    env: The TicTacToe environment instance. Used to determine action space size.\n    alpha: The learning rate for Q-value updates. Defaults to 0.1.\n    gamma: The discount factor for future rewards. Defaults to 0.9.\n    epsilon: The initial exploration rate (probability of choosing a random action).\n             Defaults to 1.0 (pure exploration initially).\n\"\"\"\n        self.env = env\n        self.alpha = alpha\n        self.gamma = gamma\n        self.epsilon = epsilon\n        self.rng = np.random.RandomState(seed=42)\n        self.q_table = {state: np.zeros(env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64) for state in self.env.state_space}\n\n    def act(self, state: np.ndarray) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select an action for the given state using the epsilon-greedy policy.\n\n    If a random number is less than epsilon, a random valid action is selected.\n    Otherwise, the action with the highest Q-value is selected. Ties are broken randomly.\n\n    Args:\n        state: The current environment observation. Can be an int or np.ndarray.\n               Must correspond to a key in the q_table.\n\n    Returns:\n        action: An integer in [0, 8] representing the chosen cell index.\n    \"\"\"\n        if self.rng.random() < self.epsilon:\n            return int(self.rng.integers(0, self.env.action_space.n))\n        \n        # Convert state to tuple for dictionary lookup\n        s_key: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(state) if not isinstance(state, tuple) else state\n        \n        q_vals: np.ndarray = self.q_table[s_key]\n        \n        # Find the best action(s)\n        max_q_val: float = np.max(q_vals)\n        best_actions: list[int] = [i for i, val in enumerate(q_vals) if abs(val - max_q_val) < 1e-06]\n        \n        # Choose randomly among best actions\n        chosen_action_idx: int = int(self.rng.choice(best_actions))\n        return int(chosen_action_idx)"

Can be an int or np.ndarray.\n        action: The action taken by the agent.\n        reward: The reward received from the environment.\n        next_state: The new environment observation after taking the action. Can be an int or np.ndarray.\n        done: Boolean indicating if the episode has terminated.\n    \"\"\"\n        # Convert states to tuples for dictionary lookup\n        s_key: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(state) if not isinstance(state, tuple) else state\n        ns_key: tuple[int, ...] = tuple(next_state) if not isinstance(next_state, tuple) else next_state\n        \n        current_q: float = self.q_table[s_key][action]\n        \n        if done:\n            max_next_q: float = 0.0\n        else:\n            # Handle case where next_state might not be in q_table (e.g., invalid move or end of game state)\n            if ns_key in self.q_table:\n                max_next_q: float = np.max(self.q_table[ns_key])\n            else:\n                max_next_q: float = 0.0\n                \n        new_q: float = current_q + self.alpha * (reward + self.gamma * max_next_q - current_q)\n        self.q_table[s_key][action] = float(new_q)"

## 1. EVOLUTIONARY ACTIONS
When Layer 3 reports a failure or Layer 1 reports a missing specialization, select exactly one decision:

- **`SPLIT_AGENT`**: When an agent repeatedly fails due to overloaded scope (e.g. split `seed_tester` into `unit_tester` + `benchmark_runner`).

  repair was sent to a different file than the one in the error, or the same error survived a previous rule.

Your rule is what those examples have in common once every file name, symbol and value is removed. Write it in this form: **"When <class of situation>, <way of working>, because <principle>."**
- **A rule describes how the agent thinks and works, never a symptom.** Not: "avoid importing `re` in config.py", "the class is `TicTacToeGame`", "close triple quotes", "use the `src.` prefix". Yes: "When a module is meant to be configuration, keep it to declarations of values; logic belongs to the modules that read the configuration, because configuration is imported everywhere and each of its dependencies spreads." Yes: "When you use a symbol from another module, take its name and signature from the contract in the payload, not from what the file name suggests, because the contract is the only source of truth about neighbours."
- **A rule earns its place in a prompt only if it changes behaviour the agent controls and the harness does not already enforce.** Every rule is read by the agent on every call, so a useless rule costs time forever. The harness rejects rules that name a file or symbol of the project, that encode an error code, exception type or line number, that concern Python syntax, the answer shape or import resolution (all enforced by the harness itself), or that repeat a rule the agent already has.

- `user_prompt`: the request the project answers.

  - `verified_do_not_touch`: parts that work and stay as they are;
  - `entrypoint`.

- `error_feedback`: what is asked of you now.

## DIAGNOSE FIRST
Read `history` before writing anything. Typical causes, and what each one needs:
- **The interface cannot be satisfied.** A docstring that contradicts the signature or another docstring, or a signature the code cannot have. Return the corrected interface in `interfaces`, with the full new source of that module. Every name another module uses stays, with its signature (`waiting_on_it` and `current_plan` show who uses what).

- **The same mistake keeps coming back.** Name it in the new description: what to write, and what the earlier attempts got wrong.
- **A dependency failed.** The vertex waits for its own re-plan; do not work around it in this one.
- **It cannot be done** (the interface and the request contradict each other, a package is missing). Say so in `gaps` rather than writing a task that will fail again.

## RULES
- Only failed vertices get new work. Never touch `verified_do_not_touch`.
- A corrected interface follows the rules of every interface of this plan:
  - every parameter typed, a return type, a docstring, every body written as `...`;
  - imports only from planned modules (by the names they declare), the standard library and `available_packages`;
  - docstrings that describe in words what each public function returns (type, shape, range), its conventions and its edge cases; no executable examples (`>>>`), a number computed in your head is usually wrong;
  - a function the harness calls (`entrypoint`, `plots`) takes no required arguments.
- Harness contracts, unchanged: the thesis is `thesis.md`; test modules are `tests/test_<module>.py`; the experiment entrypoint writes `results.csv` in the workspace root (tidy rows `method,metric,value`, optional `std_dev,n_runs`, one row per method and metric). Results and figures come from running code, so a problem with them is a task on the module that writes them, never a task on `results.csv`.
- Each task has `target_node` (the failed vertex's file), `description` (in English: the functions to write by their interface names, and what the earlier attempts got wrong) and `assigned_agent`: `seed_coder` for a module, `seed_tester` for a test file, `seed_writer` for a chapter.       "environment.py": "\"\"\"Implements the Tic-Tac-Toe game logic and a Gymnasium-compatible wrapper.\"\"\"\n\nimport gymnasium as gym\nfrom typing import Tuple, Optional\nimport numpy as np\n\n\nclass TicTacToeEnv(gym.Env):\n    \"\"\"A Gymnasium environment for the Game of Tic-Tac-Toe.\n    \n    The board is represented as a 1D array of size 9 (3x3 flattened), \n    where cells contain 0 (empty), 1 (player X), or -1 (player O).\n    Player X always moves first.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    metadata = {\"render_modes\": [\"human\", \"ansi\"]}\n\n    def __init__(self, render_mode: Optional[str] = None):\n        \"\"\"Initialize the environment.\n        \n        Args:\n            render_mode: Rendering mode string. Defaults to None (no rendering).\n        \"\"\"\n        super().__init__()\n        self.render_mode = render_mode\n        self.board_size = 9\n        self.observation_space = gym.spaces.Box(\n            low=-1, high=1, shape=(self.board_size,), dtype=np.int8\n        )\n        self.action_space = gym.spaces.Discrete(self.board_size)\n        self._state: np.ndarray = None\n        self._done: bool = False\n        self._current_player: int = 1  # 1 for X, -1 for O\n        self._seed_rng = np.random.default_rng()\n\n    def reset(\n        self, \n        seed: Optional[int] = None \n    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, dict]:\n        \"\"\"Resets the environment to the initial state.\n        \n        Args:\n            seed: Optional random seed for reproducibility. Defaults to None.\n            \n        Returns:\n            observation: The initial board state (np.ndarray of shape (9,) with dtype int8).\n            info: Auxiliary diagnostic information (empty dict).\n        \"\"\"\n        super().reset(seed=seed)\n        self._state = np.zeros(self.board_size, dtype=np.int8)\n        self._done = False\n        self._current_player = 1\n        return self._state.copy(), {}\n\n    def step(\n        self, \n        action: int \n    ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, float, bool, bool, dict]:\n        \"\"\"Performs a single environment step.\n        \n        Args:\n            action: An integer in [0, 8] representing the cell index to place a mark.\n            \n        Returns:\n            observation: The new board state (np.ndarray).\n            reward: Reward for the current player (+1 for win, 0 for draw, -1 for loss).\n            terminated: Boolean indicating if the game has ended due to win or loss.\n            truncated: Boolean indicating if the episode was truncated (e.g., max steps). Always False here.\n            info: Auxiliary diagnostic information including if the action was legal and whose turn it is.\n            \n        Raises:\n            ValueError: If the action is invalid (cell already occupied).\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._done:\n            raise RuntimeError(\"Episode must be reset before stepping again.\")\n\n        if not self.action_space.contains(action):\n            raise ValueError(f\"Invalid action {action}. Must be in [0, 8].\")\n\n        if self._state[action] != 0:\n            # Penalty for invalid move: immediate loss\n            reward = -1.0\n            terminated = True\n            info = {\n                \"valid_action\": False,\n                \"player_turn\": self._current_player,\n                \"board_copy\": self._state.copy()\n            }\n            return self._state, reward, terminated, False, info\n\n        # Apply move\n        self._state[action] = self._current_player\n        \n        # Check for termination\n        win = self._check_win(self._current_player)\n        if win:\n            reward = 1.0\n            terminated = True\n        elif np.all(self._state != 0):\n            # Draw\n            reward = 0.5  # Standard convention: half point for draw, or 0. Let's use 0.5 to distinguish from loss (-1) visually if needed, but typically 0 for draw in zero-sum games is better. \n                           # However, to make it clear it's not a win for either:\n            reward = 0.0\n            terminated = True\n        else:\n            reward = 0.0\n            terminated = False\n            self._current_player *= -1\n\n        info = {\n            \"valid_action\": True,\n            \"player_turn\": self._current_player if not terminated else 0,\n            \"board_copy\": self._state.copy()\n        }\n\n        return self._state, reward, terminated, False, info\n\n    def _check_win(self, player: int) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"Check if the specified player has won.\n        \n        Args:\n            player: The player identifier (1 or -1).\n            \n        Returns:\n            True if the player has three in a row, False otherwise.\n        \"\"\"\n        b = self._state.reshape(3, 3)\n        # Rows\n        if np.any(b.sum(axis=1) == player * 3):\n            return True\n        # Cols\n        if np.any(b.sum(axis=0) == player * 3):\n            return True\n        # Diagonals\n        if b[0, 0] == player and b[1, 1] == player and b[2, 2] == player:\n            return True\n        if b[0, 2] == player and b[1, 1] == player and b[2, 0] == player:\n            return True\n        return False\n",
      "agent.py": "\"\"\"Implements the Q-Learning agent class with standard exploration-exploitation logic (epsilon-greedy).\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom typing import Optional, Tuple\n\n# Import with string annotation to avoid circular dependency issues in some contexts,\n# but standard import is fine here if env.py is loaded.\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv\n\n# --- Constants ---\nDEFAULT_ALPHA: float = 0.1\nDEFAULT_GAMMA: float = 0.9\nDEFAULT_EPSILON_START: float = 1.0\nDEFAULT_EPSILON_END: float = 0.05\n\n\nclass QLearningAgent:\n    \"\"\"A tabular Q-Learning agent for Tic-Tac-Toe.\n    \n    The agent maintains a Q-table mapping states (board configurations) to action values.\n    It uses an epsilon-greedy policy for exploration.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        env: 'TicTacToeEnv',\n        alpha: float = DEFAULT_ALPHA,\n        gamma: float = DEFAULT_GAMMA,\n        epsilon: float = DEFAULT_EPSILON_START,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the Q-Learning agent.\n        \n        Args:\n            env: The TicTacToe environment instance. Used to determine action space size.\n            alpha: The learning rate for Q-value updates. Defaults to 0.1.\n            gamma: The discount factor for future rewards. Defaults to 0.9.\n            epsilon: The initial exploration rate (probability of choosing a random action).\n                     Defaults to 1.0 (pure exploration initially).\n        \"\"\"\n        self.env = env\n        self.alpha = alpha\n        self.gamma = gamma\n        self.epsilon = epsilon\n        \n        # Action space size is determined by the environment (9 cells)\n        num_actions = env.action_space.n\n        # Initialize Q-table with zeros. Key: state tuple, Value: array of Q-values.\n        self.q_table: dict[Tuple[int, ...], np.ndarray] = {}\n        \n        # Use modern numpy random generator\n        self.rng = np.random.default_rng()\n\n    def act(self, state: np.ndarray) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select an action for the given state using the epsilon-greedy policy.\n        \n        If a random number is less than epsilon, a random valid action is selected.\n        Otherwise, the action with the highest Q-value is selected. Ties are broken randomly.\n        \n        Args:\n            state: The current environment observation (np.ndarray of shape (9,) with dtype int8).\n                   Must contain only values from {-1, 0, 1}.\n                   \n        Returns:\n            action: An integer in [0, 8] representing the chosen cell index. Returns a standard Python int.\n        \"\"\"\n        state_key = tuple(state)\n        \n        # Initialize Q-values for new states\n        if state_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[state_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        \n        # Epsilon-greedy action selection\n        if self.rng.random() < self.epsilon:\n            # rng.integers returns a numpy scalar; .item() converts it to a Python int\n            return int(self.rng.integers(0, self.env.action_space.n).item())\n        else:\n            q_values = self.q_table[state_key]\n            # Find all actions with the maximum Q-value\n            max_q = np.max(q_values)\n            max_actions = np.where(q_values == max_q)[0]\n            # Randomly choose one of the best actions\n            idx = int(self.rng.integers(0, len(max_actions)).item())\n            return int(max_actions[idx])\n\n    def update(\n        self,\n        state: np.ndarray,\n        action: int,\n        reward: float,\n        next_state: np.ndarray,\n        done: bool,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Update the Q-value for the given state-action pair.\n        \n        Uses the standard Q-Learning update rule:\n        Q(s, a) <- Q(s, a) + alpha * (reward + gamma * max_a' Q(s', a') - Q(s, a))\n        \n        Args:\n            state: The previous environment observation.\n            action: The action taken by the agent.\n            reward: The reward received from the environment.\n            next_state: The new environment observation after taking the action.\n            done: Boolean indicating if the episode has terminated.\n        \"\"\"\n        s_key = tuple(state)\n        a_next_key = tuple(next_state)\n        \n        # Initialize Q-values for the next state if it hasn't been visited\n        if a_next_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[a_next_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        # Ensure s_key is also initialized to be safe (though act usually does this)\n        if s_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[s_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        \n        current_q = self.q_table[s_key][action]\n        \n        if done:\n            target = reward\n        else:\n            max_next_q = np.max(self.q_table[a_next_key])\n            target = reward + self.gamma * max_next_q\n            \n        self.q_table[s_key][action] += self.alpha * (target - current_q)",
      "baseline_agent.py": "\"\"\"Implements the random baseline agent that selects uniformly from valid moves.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom typing import Optional, TYPE_CHECKING\n\nif TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from environment import TicTacToeEnv\n\n\nclass RandomAgent:\n    \"\"\"A dummy agent that chooses a legal move at random for baseline comparison.\n\n    Attributes:\n        env: The Tic-Tac-Toe environment instance used to determine board size and rules.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, env: \"TicTacToeEnv\") -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize the random agent.\n\n        Args:\n            env: The Tic-TacToe environment instance. Stored to query valid actions.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.env = env\n\n    def act(self, state: np.ndarray) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select a valid action uniformly at random from the legal moves in ``state``.\n\n        Args:\n            state: Current board observation (numpy array of shape (9,)).\n                   Must contain values 0 (empty), 1 (X), -1 (O).\n\n        Returns:\n            action: Integer index in [0, 8] corresponding to an empty cell on the board.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Identify empty cells (value == 0)\n        empty_indices = np.where(state == 0)[0]\n        if len(empty_indices) == 0:\n            raise ValueError(\"No empty cells available for action.\")\n        return int(np.random.choice(empty_indices))\n",
      "experiment.py": "\"\"\"Orchestrates the training of the Q-Learning agent and its evaluation against both itself (during play) and the random baseline, aggregating results into a CSV file.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import List, Tuple, Dict\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom environment import TicTacToeEnv\nfrom agent import QLearningAgent\nfrom baseline_agent import RandomAgent\n\n# --- Constants ---\nN_EPISODES: int = 1000\nRANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES: int = 1000\nSEED: int = 42\nEpsilonDecayRate: float = 0.995\nMinEpsilon: float = 0.01\nOUTPUT_CSV: str = \"results.csv\"\nWORKSPACE_ROOT: Path = Path(\".\")\n\n\ndef run_experiment() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run the full reinforcement learning experiment and save results to CSV.\n\n    This function performs three main phases:\n    1. Training: The Q-Learning agent plays against a random opponent for \n       ``N_EPISODES`` episodes, updating its Q-table after each move.\n    2. Baseline Evaluation: A game played between two RandomAgents is simulated \n       for ``RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES`` games to establish a win/draw/loss distribution \n       for purely random play.\n    3. Final Evaluation: The trained Q-Learning agent plays against the same \n       RandomAgent for ``RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES`` games to measure its performance.\n\n    Results are aggregated into rows with columns: \n    ``method, metric, value, std_dev, n_runs``.\n    Methods are \"Q-Learning_vs_Random\" and \"Random_vs_Random\". Metrics are \n    \"win_rate\", \"draw_rate\", \"loss_rate\" (relative to the agent named first). \n\n    The output CSV is written to the workspace root at ``results.csv``.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = TicTacToeEnv()\n    \n    # Initialize Q-Learning Agent\n    agent = QLearningAgent(\n        env=env,\n        epsilon=1.0\n    )\n    \n    # Initialize Random Agents for baseline and evaluation\n    random_agent_eval = RandomAgent(env)\n    random_agent_baseline_1 = RandomAgent(env)\n    random_agent_baseline_2 = RandomAgent(env)\n    \n    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)\n\n    # --- Phase 1: Training ---\n    for episode in range(N_EPISODES):\n        state, _ = env.reset(seed=SEED + episode)\n        done = False\n        \n        while not done:\n            action = agent.act(state)\n            next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            agent.update(state, action, reward, next_state, done)\n            state = next_state\n            \n            # Decay epsilon\n            if agent.epsilon > MinEpsilon:\n                agent.epsilon *= EpsilonDecayRate\n\n    # --- Phase 2: Baseline Evaluation (Random vs Random) ---\n    baseline_results = _evaluate_agent(\n        env=env,\n        p1_agent=random_agent_baseline_1,\n        p2_agent=random_agent_baseline_2,\n        n_games=RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES,\n        rng=rng\n    )\n    \n    # --- Phase 3: Trained Agent Evaluation (Q-Learning vs Random) ---\n    trained_results = _evaluate_agent(\n        env=env,\n        p1_agent=agent,\n        p2_agent=random_agent_eval,\n        n_games=RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES,\n        rng=rng\n    )\n\n    # Must have ``act(state)``.\n        p2_agent: The agent playing as Player O. Must have ``act(state)``.\n        n_games: Number of games to simulate.\n        rng: Random number generator for reproducibility.\n\n    Returns:\n        A dictionary with keys 'p1_wins', 'p2_wins', 'draws', each mapping to the \n        count of such outcomes observed during the evaluation.\n    \"\"\"\n    p1_wins = 0\n    p2_wins = 0\n    draws = 0\n\n    for i in range(n_games):\n        state, _ = env.reset(seed=rng.integers(0, 10000))\n        done = False\n        last_winner = None \n\n        while not done:\n            if env._current_player == 1:\n                action = p1_agent.act(state)\n            else:\n                action = p2_agent.act(state)\n                \n            next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            \n            # Determine who got what reward. \n            # Reward is from the perspective of the player making the move.\n            if terminated:\n                if reward == 1.0:\n                    # The current mover won\n                    if env._current_player != (-2): # Check logic below carefully based on env step implementation\n                        # In TicTacToeEnv.step, reward is given to self._current_player who just moved.\n                        # But after the move, _current_player switches or stays? \n                        # Env code: self._state[action] = self._current_player.       "plots.py": "\"\"\"Reads experimental results from CSV and generates visualizations of learning curves and win rate comparisons.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nfrom typing import List\n\nimport matplotlib\nmatplotlib.use('Agg')\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nimport seaborn as sns\n\n# Constants for experiment reproducibility and styling\nFIGURE_DIR: str = \"figures\"\nRESULTS_FILE: str = \"results.csv\"\n\n\ndef generate_plots() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Generate plots from experimental results and save them to disk.\n\n    Reads the ``results.csv`` file (written by :func:`experiment.run_experiment`) \n    which must contain columns: 'method', 'metric', 'value'. The CSV is expected to \n    contain rows for win_rate, draw_rate, loss_rate, mean_reward, and std_dev for \n    each method (e.g., 'q_learning', 'random_baseline').\n\n    Creates two figures:\n    1. **Distribution Comparison**: A grouped bar chart comparing the rates of \n       winning, drawing, and losing between the Q-Learning agent and the Baseline.\n    2. **Reward Statistics**: A bar chart comparing the mean reward and standard \n       deviation between the methods.\n\n    Saves figures to ``figures/`` directory (creating it if necessary).\n    \"\"\"\n    # Load data\n    if not os.path.exists(RESULTS_FILE):\n        raise FileNotFoundError(\n            f\"Results file '{RESULTS_FILE}' not found. Run experiment first.\"\n        )\n    \n    df: pd.DataFrame = pd.read_csv(RESULTS_FILE)\n    \n    # Ensure columns exist\n    required_cols: List[str] = ['method', 'metric', 'value']\n    for col in required_cols:\n        if col not in df.columns:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Missing required column '{col}' in {RESULTS_FILE}\")\n\n    # Prepare directories\n    os.makedirs(FIGURE_DIR, exist_ok=True)\n\n    # --- Plot 1: Win/Loss/Draw Distribution Comparison ---\n    _plot_distribution_comparison(df)\n\n    # --- Plot 2: Mean Reward and Std Dev Bar Chart ---\n    _plot_reward_metrics(df)\n\n\ndef _plot_distribution_comparison(df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Visualize win, draw, and loss rates for each method.\n    \n    Args:\n        df: DataFrame containing aggregated results from experiment.csv.\n            Must contain rows for 'win_rate', 'draw_rate', 'loss_rate' per method.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Filter for distribution metrics\n    dist_metrics: List[str] = ['win_rate', 'draw_rate', 'loss_rate']\n    df_dist: pd.DataFrame = df[df['metric'].isin(dist_metrics)].copy()\n    \n    if df_dist.empty:\n        print(\"Warning: No distribution metrics found in results for plotting.\")\n        return\n\n    # Pivot to get rates as columns indexed by method\n    plot_data: pd.DataFrame = df_dist.pivot(index='method', columns='metric', values='value')\n    \n    # Reindex to ensure correct order if some methods miss a metric (unlikely in this harness)\n    for m in dist_metrics:\n        if m not in plot_data.columns:\n            plot_data[m] = 0.0\n    \n    plot_data = plot_data[dist_metrics]\n\n    ax: plt.Axes\n    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n    \n    # Plot grouped bars\n    x_vals: np.ndarray = np.arange(len(plot_data.index))\n    width: float = 0.25\n    methods: List[str] = plot_data.index.tolist()\n    metric_colors = {\n        'win_rate': '#1f77b4',\n        'draw_rate': '#ff7f0e',\n        'loss_rate': '#d62728'\n    }\n\n    for i, metric in enumerate(dist_metrics):\n        if metric in plot_data.columns:\n            ax.bar(\n                x_vals + i * width - width,\n                plot_data[metric],\n                width,\n                label=metric.replace('_', ' ').title(),\n                color=metric_colors[metric],\n                edgecolor='black'\n            )\n    \n    ax.set_xticks(x_vals)\n    ax.set_xticklabels([m.replace('_', '\\n') for m in methods], fontsize=10)\n    ax.set_ylabel('Rate (0-1)')\n    ax.set_title('Win, Draw, and Loss Rates Comparison')\n    ax.legend(loc='lower right')\n    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05)\n    ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n\n    plt.tight_layout()\n    plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURE_DIR, 'distribution_comparison.png'), dpi=150)\n    plt.close(fig)\n\n\ndef _plot_reward_metrics(df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Visualize Mean Reward and Std Dev for each method.\n    \n    Args:\n        df: DataFrame containing aggregated results from experiment.csv.\n            Must contain rows for 'mean_reward' and 'std_dev' per method.\n    \"\"\"\n    reward_metrics: List[str] = ['mean_reward', 'std_dev']\n    df_reward: pd.DataFrame = df[df['metric'].isin(reward_metrics)].copy()\n\n    if df_reward.empty:\n        print(\"Warning: No reward metrics found in results for plotting.\")\n        return\n\n    # Pivot\n    plot_data: pd.DataFrame = df_reward.pivot(index='method', columns='metric', values='value')\n    \n    # Handle missing std_dev (often 0 or not computed if n_runs=1)\n    if 'std_dev' not in plot_data.columns:\n        plot_data['std_dev'] = 0.0\n        print(\"Note: Standard deviation data was missing, defaulted to 0.0.\")\n    \n    plot_data = plot_data[['mean_reward', 'std_dev']]\n\n    ax: plt.Axes\n    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n    \n    x_vals: np.ndarray = np.arange(len(plot_data.index))\n    width: float = 0.35\n\n    bars1 = ax.bar(\n        x_vals - width/2,\n        plot_data['mean_reward'],\n        width,\n        label='Mean Reward',\n        color='#1f77b4',\n        edgecolor='black'\n    )\n    \n    # Plot error bars or a secondary bar for std_dev. A secondary bar is clearer for magnitude.\n    bars2 = ax.bar(\n        x_vals + width/2,\n        plot_data['std_dev'],\n        width,\n        label='Std Dev',\n        color='#ff7f0e',\n        edgecolor='black'\n    )\n\n    ax.set_xticks(x_vals)\n    ax.set_xticklabels([m.replace('_', '\\n') for m in plot_data.index], fontsize=10)\n    ax.set_ylabel('Value')\n    ax.set_title('Mean Reward and Standard Deviation')\n    ax.legend(loc='best')\n    ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n\n    plt.tight_layout()\n    plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURE_DIR, 'reward_metrics.png'), dpi=150)\n    plt.close(fig)"
    },

   - **Results Format (tidy CSV)**: the entrypoint writes `results.csv` in the workspace root (no subdirectory, no other name), rows `method,metric,value` (optional `std_dev,n_runs`), exactly one row per method and metric: repetitions are aggregated into that row (mean, `std_dev`, `n_runs`), never written as a row per run or seed. The metrics are the ones declared in the plan; the column set stays fixed (the harness rejects other columns and repeated rows).
4. **Cross-File Symbol Consistency**:
   - Use the signatures in `specification` when you call other modules; do not guess them.
   - Test files (`test_*.py`) belong to `seed_tester`. If a test looks wrong to you, say so in `summary` instead of rewriting it.

Used to determine action space size.\n            alpha: The learning rate for Q-value updates. Defaults to 0.1.\n            gamma: The discount factor for future rewards. Defaults to 0.9.\n            epsilon: The initial exploration rate (probability of choosing a random action).\n                     Defaults to 1.0 (pure exploration initially).\n        \"\"\"\n        self.env = env\n        self.alpha = alpha\n        self.gamma = gamma\n        self.epsilon = epsilon\n        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)\n        self.q_table: dict[Tuple[int, ...], np.ndarray] = {state: np.zeros(env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64) for state in self.env.state_space}\n\n    def act(self, state: int | np.ndarray) -> int:\n        \"\"\"Select an action for the given state using the epsilon-greedy policy.\n\n        If a random number is less than epsilon, a random valid action is selected.\n        Otherwise, the action with the highest Q-value is selected. Ties are broken randomly.\n\n        Args:\n            state: The current environment observation. Can be an int or np.ndarray.\n                   Must correspond to a key in the q_table.\n\n        Returns:\n            action: A standard Python integer in [0, 8] representing the chosen cell index.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self.rng.random() < self.epsilon:\n            s_key: tuple[int, ...] = self._normalize_state(state)\n            valid_actions: list[int] = [i for i in range(self.env.action_space.n) if self.env.is_valid_move(s_key, i)]\n            if not valid_actions:\n                return 0\n            chosen_action_idx: int = self.rng.choice(valid_actions).item()\n            return chosen_action_idx\n        s_key: tuple[int, ...] = self._normalize_state(state)\n        q_vals: np.ndarray = self.q_table[s_key]\n        max_q_val: float = np.max(q_vals)\n        best_actions: list[int] = [i for i, val in enumerate(q_vals) if abs(val - max_q_val) < 1e-06]\n        chosen_action_idx: int = self.rng.choice(best_actions).item()\n        return chosen_action_idx\n\n    def update(self, state: int | np.ndarray, action: int, reward: float, next_state: int | np.ndarray, done: bool) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Update the Q-value for the given state-action pair.\n\n        Uses the standard Q-Learning update rule:\n        Q(s, a) <- Q(s, a) + alpha * (reward + gamma * max_a' Q(s', a') - Q(s, a))\n\n        Args:\n            state: The previous environment observation. Can be an int or np.ndarray.\n            action: The action taken by the agent.\n            reward: The reward received from the environment.\n            next_state: The new environment observation after taking the action. Can be an int or np.ndarray.\n            done: Boolean indicating if the episode has terminated.\n        \"\"\"\n        s_key: tuple[int, ...] = self._normalize_state(state)\n        ns_key: tuple[int, ...] = self._normalize_state(next_state)\n        if s_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[s_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        if ns_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[ns_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        current_q: float = self.q_table[s_key][action]\n        if done:\n            max_next_q: float = 0.0\n        elif ns_key in self.q_table:\n            max_next_q: float = float(np.max(self.q_table[ns_key]))\n        else:\n            max_next_q: float = 0.0\n        new_q: float = current_q + self.alpha * (reward + self.gamma * max_next_q - current_q)\n        self.q_table[s_key][action] = new_q\n\n    def _normalize_state(self, state: int | np.ndarray) -> tuple[int, ...]:\n        \"\"\"Convert the given state to a tuple of integers for dictionary keys.\n\n        Handles both integer and numpy array inputs by converting them to tuples.\n\n        Args:\n            state: The environment observation. - `error_feedback`: what is asked of you now.

## DIAGNOSE FIRST
Read `history` before writing anything. Typical causes, and what each one needs:
- **The interface cannot be satisfied.** A docstring that contradicts the signature or another docstring, or a signature the code cannot have. Return the corrected interface in `interfaces`, with the full new source of that module. Every name another module uses stays, with its signature (`waiting_on_it` and `current_plan` show who uses what).
- **The task asked for too much in one answer.** Split it into smaller tasks, one function or method each, in dependency order.
- **The same mistake keeps coming back.** Name it in the new description: what to write, and what the earlier attempts got wrong.
- **A dependency failed.** The vertex waits for its own re-plan; do not work around it in this one.
- **It cannot be done** (the interface and the request contradict each other, a package is missing). Say so in `gaps` rather than writing a task that will fail again.

## RULES
- Only failed vertices get new work. Never touch `verified_do_not_touch`.
- A corrected interface follows the rules of every interface of this plan:
  - every parameter typed, a return type, a docstring, every body written as `...`;
  - imports only from planned modules (by the names they declare), the standard library and `available_packages`;
  - docstrings that describe in words what each public function returns (type, shape, range), its conventions and its edge cases; no executable examples (`>>>`), a number computed in your head is usually wrong;
  - a function the harness calls (`entrypoint`, `plots`) takes no required arguments.
- Harness contracts, unchanged: the thesis is `thesis.md`; test modules are `tests/test_<module>.py`; the experiment entrypoint writes `results.csv` in the workspace root (tidy rows `method,metric,value`, optional `std_dev,n_runs`, one row per method and metric). Results and figures come from running code, so a problem with them is a task on the module that writes them, never a task on `results.csv`.
- Each task has `target_node` (the failed vertex's file), `description` (in English: the functions to write by their interface names, and what the earlier attempts got wrong) and `assigned_agent`: `seed_coder` for a module, `seed_tester` for a test file, `seed_writer` for a chapter. A chapter task says "Chapter N" with the index from `planned_chapters`.
- Titles of chapters stay in Polish; everything else you write is English.

Return strictly one JSON object, no text outside it:

  "interfaces": {"<module path>.py": "<full new interface source>"},
  "gaps": [{"vertex": "<failed vertex>", "reason": "<why it cannot be done>"}]
}
```
`interfaces` and `gaps` are omitted when empty.

Returns a standard Python int.\n        \"\"\"\n        state_key = tuple(state)\n        \n        # Initialize Q-values for new states if not present\n        if state_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[state_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        \n        q_values = self.q_table[state_key]\n        \n        # Epsilon-greedy action selection\n        if self.rng.random() < self.epsilon:\n            # Select uniformly from all actions (assuming environment will validate or agent handles invalid moves)\n            # In this implementation, we assume valid states are passed. If state is full, this returns 0.\n            return int(self.rng.integers(0, self.env.action_space.n).item())\n        else:\n            # Find all actions with the maximum Q-value\n            max_q = np.max(q_values)\n            # Use boolean mask for robustness against floating point issues\n            max_actions = np.where(q_values == max_q)[0]\n            # Randomly choose one of the best actions\n            idx = int(self.rng.integers(0, len(max_actions)).item())\n            return int(max_actions[idx])\n\n    def update(\n        self,\n        state: np.ndarray,\n        action: int,\n        reward: float,\n        next_state: np.ndarray,\n        done: bool,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Update the Q-value for the given state-action pair.\n        \n        Uses the standard Q-Learning update rule:\n        Q(s, a) <- Q(s, a) + alpha * (reward + gamma * max_a' Q(s', a') - Q(s, a))\n        \n        Args:\n            state: The previous environment observation.\n            action: The action taken by the agent.\n            reward: The reward received from the environment.\n            next_state: The new environment observation after taking the action.\n            done: Boolean indicating if the episode has terminated.\n        \"\"\"\n        s_key = tuple(state)\n        ns_key = tuple(next_state)\n        \n        # Initialize Q-values for current state if not present\n        if s_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[s_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n            \n        # Initialize Q-values for next state if not present\n        if ns_key not in self.q_table:\n            self.q_table[ns_key] = np.zeros(self.env.action_space.n, dtype=np.float64)\n        \n        current_q = self.q_table[s_key][action]\n        \n        if done:\n            target = reward\n        else:\n            max_next_q = float(np.max(self.q_table[ns_key]))\n            target = reward + self.gamma * max_next_q\n            \n        self.q_table[s_key][action] += self.alpha * (target - current_q)",

Metrics are \n    \"win_rate\", \"draw_rate\", \"loss_rate\" (relative to the agent named first). \n\n    The output CSV is written to the workspace root at ``results.csv``.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = TicTacToeEnv()\n    \n    # Initialize Q-Learning Agent\n    agent = QLearningAgent(\n        env=env,\n        epsilon=1.0\n    )\n    \n    # Initialize Random Agents for baseline and evaluation\n    random_agent_eval = RandomAgent(env)\n    random_agent_baseline_1 = RandomAgent(env)\n    random_agent_baseline_2 = RandomAgent(env)\n    \n    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)\n\n    # --- Phase 1: Training ---\n    for episode in range(N_EPISODES):\n        state, _ = env.reset(seed=SEED + episode)\n        done = False\n        \n        while not done:\n            action = agent.act(state)\n            next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            agent.update(state, action, reward, next_state, done)\n            state = next_state\n            \n            # --- Phase 3: Trained Agent Evaluation (Q-Learning vs Random) ---\n    trained_results = _evaluate_agent(\n        env=env,\n        p1_agent=agent,\n        p2_agent=random_agent_eval,\n        n_games=RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES,\n        rng=rng\n    )\n\n    # Q-Learning Rows (Trained vs Random)\n    rows.append([\"Q-Learning_vs_Random\", \"win_rate\", f\"{trained_results['p1_wins'] / RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES:.4f}\", \"0\", str(RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES)])\n    rows.append([\"Q-Learning_vs_Random\", \"draw_rate\", f\"{trained_results['draws'] / RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES:.4f}\", \"0\", str(RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES)])\n    rows.append([\"Q-Learning_vs_Random\", \"loss_rate\", f\"{trained_results['p1_losses'] / RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES:.4f}\", \"0\", str(RANDOM_BASLINE_GAMES)])\n\n    output_path = WORKSPACE_ROOT / OUTPUT_CSV\n    with open(output_path, mode='w', newline='') as csvfile:\n        writer = csv.writer(csvfile)\n        writer.writerow([\"method\", \"metric\", \"value\", \"std_dev\", \"n_runs\"])\n        writer.writerows(rows)\n\n\ndef _evaluate_agent(\n    env: TicTacToeEnv,\n    p1_agent, \n    p2_agent,\n    n_games: int,\n    rng: np.random.Generator\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"Evaluate an agent playing as player 1 against another agent (player 2).\n\n    Args:\n        env: The TicTacToe environment instance.\n        p1_agent: The agent playing as Player X (moves first). Must have ``act(state)``.\n        p2_agent: The agent playing as Player O. Must have ``act(state)``.\n        n_games: Number of games to simulate.\n        rng: Random number generator for reproducibility.\n\n    Returns:\n        A dictionary with keys 'p1_wins', 'p2_wins', 'draws', each mapping to the \n        count of such outcomes observed during the evaluation.\n    \"\"\"\n    p1_wins = 0\n    p2_wins = 0\n    draws = 0\n\n    for i in range(n_games):\n        state, _ = env.reset(seed=rng.integers(0, 10000))\n        done = False\n        last_winner = None \n\n        while not done:\n            if env._current_player == 1:\n                action = p1_agent.act(state)\n            else:\n                action = p2_agent.act(state)\n                \n            next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)\n            done = terminated or truncated\n            \n            # Determine who got what reward. \n            # Reward is from the perspective of the player making the move.\n            if terminated:\n                if reward == 1.0:\n                    # The current mover won\n                    if env._current_player != (-2): # Check logic below carefully based on env step implementation\n                        # In TicTacToeEnv.step, reward is given to self._current_player who just moved.\n                        # But after the move, _current_player switches or stays? \n                        # Env code: self._state[action] = self._current_player. No, immediate loss here)\n                    if env._current_player == 1: p2_wins += 1\n                    else: p1_wins += 1\n                else:\n                    # Draw\n                    draws += 1\n            \n            state = next_state\n\n    return {\n        \"p1_wins\": p1_wins,\n        \"p2_wins\": p2_wins,\n        \"draws\": draws\n    }",
      "plots.py": "\"\"\"Reads experimental results from CSV and generates visualizations of learning curves and win rate comparisons.\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nfrom typing import List\n\nimport matplotlib\nmatplotlib.use('Agg')\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nimport seaborn as sns\n\n# Constants for experiment reproducibility and styling\nFIGURE_DIR: str = \"figures\"\nRESULTS_FILE: str = \"results.csv\"\n\n\ndef generate_plots() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Generate plots from experimental results and save them to disk.\n\n    Reads the ``results.csv`` file (written by :func:`experiment.run_experiment`) \n    which must contain columns: 'method', 'metric', 'value'. The CSV is expected to \n    contain rows for win_rate, draw_rate, loss_rate, mean_reward, and std_dev for \n    each method (e.g., 'q_learning', 'random_baseline').\n\n    Creates two figures:\n    1. **Distribution Comparison**: A grouped bar chart comparing the rates of \n       winning, drawing, and losing between the Q-Learning agent and the Baseline.\n    2. **Reward Statistics**: A bar chart comparing the mean reward and standard \n       deviation between the methods.\n\n    Saves figures to ``figures/`` directory (creating it if necessary).\n    \"\"\"\n    # Load data\n    if not os.path.exists(RESULTS_FILE):\n        raise FileNotFoundError(\n            f\"Results file '{RESULTS_FILE}' not found. Run experiment first.\"\n        )\n    \n    df: pd.DataFrame = pd.read_csv(RESULTS_FILE)\n    \n    # Ensure columns exist\n    required_cols: List[str] = ['method', 'metric', 'value']\n    for col in required_cols:\n        if col not in df.columns:\n            raise ValueError(f\"Missing required column '{col}' in {RESULTS_FILE}\")\n\n    # Prepare directories\n    os.makedirs(FIGURE_DIR, exist_ok=True)\n\n    # --- Plot 1: Win/Loss/Draw Distribution Comparison ---\n    _plot_distribution_comparison(df)\n\n    # --- Plot 2: Mean Reward and Std Dev Bar Chart ---\n    _plot_reward_metrics(df)\n\n\ndef _plot_distribution_comparison(df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Visualize win, draw, and loss rates for each method.\n    \n    Args:\n        df: DataFrame containing aggregated results from experiment.csv.\n            Must contain rows for 'win_rate', 'draw_rate', 'loss_rate' per method.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Filter for distribution metrics\n    dist_metrics: List[str] = ['win_rate', 'draw_rate', 'loss_rate']\n    df_dist: pd.DataFrame = df[df['metric'].isin(dist_metrics)].copy()\n    \n    if df_dist.empty:\n        print(\"Warning: No distribution metrics found in results for plotting.\")\n        return\n\n    # Pivot to get rates as columns indexed by method\n    plot_data: pd.DataFrame = df_dist.pivot(index='method', columns='metric', values='value')\n    \n    # Reindex to ensure correct order if some methods miss a metric (unlikely in this harness)\n    for m in dist_metrics:\n        if m not in plot_data.columns:\n            plot_data[m] = 0.0\n    \n    plot_data = plot_data[dist_metrics]\n\n    ax: plt.Axes\n    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n    \n    # Plot grouped bars\n    x_vals: np.ndarray = np.arange(len(plot_data.index))\n    width: float = 0.25\n    methods: List[str] = plot_data.index.tolist()\n    metric_colors = {\n        'win_rate': '#1f77b4',\n        'draw_rate': '#ff7f0e',\n        'loss_rate': '#d62728'\n    }\n\n    for i, metric in enumerate(dist_metrics):\n        if metric in plot_data.columns:\n            ax.bar(\n                x_vals + i * width - width,\n                plot_data[metric],\n                width,\n                label=metric.replace('_', ' ').title(),\n                color=metric_colors[metric],\n                edgecolor='black'\n            )\n    \n    ax.set_xticks(x_vals)\n    ax.set_xticklabels([m.replace('_', '\\n') for m in methods], fontsize=10)\n    ax.set_ylabel('Rate (0-1)')\n    ax.set_title('Win, Draw, and Loss Rates Comparison')\n    ax.legend(loc='lower right')\n    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05)\n    ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n\n    plt.tight_layout()\n    plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURE_DIR, 'distribution_comparison.png'), dpi=150)\n    plt.close(fig)\n\n\ndef _plot_reward_metrics(df: pd.DataFrame) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Visualize Mean Reward and Std Dev for each method.\n    \n    Args:\n        df: DataFrame containing aggregated results from experiment.csv.\n            Must contain rows for 'mean_reward' and 'std_dev' per method.\n    \"\"\"\n    reward_metrics: List[str] = ['mean_reward', 'std_dev']\n    df_reward: pd.DataFrame = df[df['metric'].isin(reward_metrics)].copy()\n\n    if df_reward.empty:\n        print(\"Warning: No reward metrics found in results for plotting.\")\n        return\n\n    # Pivot\n    plot_data: pd.DataFrame = df_reward.pivot(index='method', columns='metric', values='value')\n    \n    # Handle missing std_dev (often 0 or not computed if n_runs=1)\n    if 'std_dev' not in plot_data.columns:\n        plot_data['std_dev'] = 0.0\n        print(\"Note: Standard deviation data was missing, defaulted to 0.0.\")\n    \n    plot_data = plot_data[['mean_reward', 'std_dev']]\n\n    ax: plt.Axes\n    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n    \n    x_vals: np.ndarray = np.arange(len(plot_data.index))\n    width: float = 0.35\n\n    bars1 = ax.bar(\n        x_vals - width/2,\n        plot_data['mean_reward'],\n        width,\n        label='Mean Reward',\n        color='#1f77b4',\n        edgecolor='black'\n    )\n    \n    # Plot error bars or a secondary bar for std_dev. A secondary bar is clearer for magnitude.\n    bars2 = ax.bar(\n        x_vals + width/2,\n        plot_data['std_dev'],\n        width,\n        label='Std Dev',\n        color='#ff7f0e',\n        edgecolor='black'\n    )\n\n    ax.set_xticks(x_vals)\n    ax.set_xticklabels([m.replace('_', '\\n') for m in plot_data.index], fontsize=10)\n    ax.set_ylabel('Value')\n    ax.set_title('Mean Reward and Standard Deviation')\n    ax.legend(loc='best')\n    ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)\n\n    plt.tight_layout()\n    plt.savefig(os.path.join(FIGURE_DIR, 'reward_metrics.png'), dpi=150)\n    plt.close(fig)"
    },
